issue_text: I’m Elena Brooks. Before we change anything, can you tell me the car rental cancellation policy in general for my Las Vegas trip? I want to know whether I’d be charged anything if I cancel.
summary: A ten-turn travel-cancellation session for Elena Brooks: the agent explains the car-rental policy (T1), confirms rental CR-68B7 details (T2), previews then executes its cancellation (T3-T4), repeats the same policy → details → preview → cancel cycle for hotel HR-68D9 (T5-T8), and closes with two reservation-status audits (T9-T10). The run is the most internally coherent of the baseline set: at T2 and T6 the agent explicitly recalls prior tool output ("I already retrieved the full details... in the previous step") rather than re-fetching — a genuine working-memory move, and consistent with the component_timeline showing zero tool calls on exactly those two turns. The policy reasoning is sound: it correctly maps the June-15-to-September-18 gap onto the free-cancellation windows (24h car, 48h hotel) and sums the refunds to $436. As a CONTROL baseline the main uncorrected defect is the recurring "cancellation is complete and verified" claim (T4, T8) — the timeline logs only generic other calls, so the "verified" status and the post-cancel refund amounts are self-reported rather than read back from a confirmation.

|---|---|

Let me know if you'd like to go ahead with the cancellation or if you have any other questions.

findings.title: Working-memory recall done right
findings.body: T2 and T6 open with "I already retrieved/pulled the full details... in the previous step" and fire no tools — the only turns in the baseline set where a Memory › Read-from-working-memory move is both claimed and matched by a zero-tool timeline entry.

findings.title: Policy inference is grounded in dates, not fabricated
findings.body: Each preview turn carries a Reasoning › Inferring move tying the specific date gap ("more than 24/48 hours from today") to the fee outcome — a real if-then chain, distinct from the ungrounded confirmations elsewhere in the set.

findings.title: 'Complete and verified' is still self-asserted
findings.body: T4 and T8 both say the cancellation is "complete and verified", an Evaluate › Confirm move, but no retrieval call backs the post-cancel status read-back — the one place the otherwise-coherent run slips into unverified confirmation.
